description: French vocabulary register audit list. 'formal' = written-only or archaic item dead in conversation; 'preferred' = what French speakers actually say. Deck defaults: tu/vous by context, passé composé in dialogue, on for casual 'we'. Severity: 'high' = dead in speech, swap wherever it appears in conversational cards; 'medium' = written-leaning, swap in beginner content. See docs/french-register-policy.md.

dead_in_speech.rationale: Written-French tense, negation, and connector machinery that never occurs in conversation.

entries.formal: passé simple in dialogue (il alla, elle fit, nous fûmes)
entries.preferred: passé composé (il est allé, elle a fait, on a été)
entries.note: Written-narrative tense. Fine in Q4 reading/narrative cards taught as such; never in dialogue.
Archaic/literary negation; survives only in fixed regional or jocular use.
«nous allons au cinéma» → «on va au ciné» in speech. nous stays in formal speech/writing and as object/stressed pronoun — exempt those.
Formal purpose connector; conversation uses pour (que).
car is normal in writing but stiff in casual speech. Only flag in conversational cards.
